concepts.name: entity.date_established

concepts.name: entity.charity_beneficiary_category
concepts.definition: Beneficiary groups the charity reports assisting; emit each affirmative indicator as a category without treating blanks as negative claims.

concepts.name: licence.number
concepts.definition: Identifier allocated to an Australian Financial Services licensee; retain the identifier as a string, including any leading zeros.

concepts.name: licence.register_entry_name
concepts.definition: Name displayed for a licensee entry on the Australian Financial Services Licensee Register; may be an organisation name or an individual's displayed name.

concepts.name: licence.start_date
concepts.definition: Start or issue date of an Australian Financial Services licence, distinct from a licensee's company registration date; parse as a date.

concepts.name: licence.pre_fsr_reference
concepts.definition: Prior register identifier and licence number recorded for a licensee where a register was superseded by Financial Services Reform; retain each reference as supplied.

concepts.name: licence.authorisation_condition
concepts.definition: Current condition stating financial services or products authorised under the licence; retain each source condition or row as a separate observation.

concepts.name: registration.registered_business_name
concepts.definition: Business name shown on an ASIC Business Names register entry; trim surrounding whitespace and do not infer a legal-entity owner.

concepts.name: registration.business_name_status
concepts.definition: Status label of the ASIC business-name registration; trim and retain source labels without mapping them to legal-entity status.

concepts.name: registration.business_name_registration_date
concepts.definition: Date on which the business name started, parsed from the documented day/month/year format; not a company registration date.

concepts.name: registration.business_name_cancellation_date
concepts.definition: Date on which the business name ceased, parsed from the documented day/month/year format when supplied; not an entity deregistration date.

concepts.name: registration.former_state_number
concepts.definition: Identifier allocated to a business name by a previous state or territory regulator before 28 May 2012; retain the source string.

concepts.name: registration.previous_state_of_registration
concepts.definition: Abbreviated state or territory in which the business name was registered by a previous regulator; trim and accept documented abbreviations.

concepts.name: registration.business_name_abn
concepts.definition: ABN claim displayed on an ASIC business-name register entry; preserve as an entry-level identifier and do not infer legal-entity ownership.

concepts.name: entity.asic_company_type
concepts.definition: ASIC Company Dataset type code for a company or registered body; trim surrounding whitespace and accept documented codes.

concepts.name: entity.asic_company_class
concepts.definition: ASIC Company Dataset liability class code; trim surrounding whitespace and accept documented codes.

concepts.name: entity.asic_company_sub_class
concepts.definition: ASIC Company Dataset subclass code; trim surrounding whitespace and accept documented codes.

concepts.name: entity.asic_register_status
concepts.definition: Status code reported for a company in the ASIC Company Dataset; trim and preserve the source code without translating to a broader status.

concepts.name: registration.original_state
concepts.definition: State in which the company was originally registered, as reported by the ASIC Company Dataset; trim and retain the source abbreviation.

concepts.name: registration.state_registration_number
concepts.definition: Number assigned when the company was originally registered by a state; preserve as a string because formats vary by state.

concepts.name: registration.company_deregistration_date
concepts.definition: Date on which the company was deregistered, as reported by the ASIC Company Dataset; parse as a date and keep distinct from other registration regimes.

concepts.name: entity.current_name_indicator
concepts.definition: Flag stating whether the company name on an ASIC record is identified as the current name; map Y to true and blank to unknown.

concepts.name: registration.current_name_start_date
concepts.definition: Start date reported for the current registered company name; parse as a date and keep distinct from company registration date.

concepts.name: financial_period.reporting_period
concepts.definition: Income-year label associated with reported corporate tax information, retained as supplied (for example, 2023-24); trim surrounding whitespace.

concepts.name: service_location.code
concepts.definition: Source identifier for an employment-services provider site or service location; trim and preserve as a string.

concepts.name: service_location.contract_name
concepts.definition: Contract name recorded in an employment-services location record; trim without asserting the provider's legal relationship to the contract.

concepts.name: service_location.name
concepts.definition: Name used by the source for an employment-services service location; trim surrounding whitespace.

concepts.name: service_location.address_line
concepts.definition: Street or premises address line recorded for a service location; trim without inferring omitted address components.

concepts.name: service_location.website
concepts.definition: Website URL explicitly recorded for a service location; retain as a location-scoped source claim, not an entity-wide website.

concepts.name: service_location.latitude
concepts.definition: Latitude coordinate of the service location, parsed as a decimal and limited to the valid latitude range.

concepts.name: service_location.longitude
concepts.definition: Longitude coordinate of the service location, parsed as a decimal and limited to the valid longitude range.

concepts.name: service_location.agent_freecall_phone
concepts.definition: Telephone number identified as an agent free-call number in the service-location source; trim and retain as a string to preserve dialing characters and zeros.

concepts.name: contact.phone
concepts.definition: Telephone number explicitly identified as a contact phone for a service site; trim and retain as a string without treating it as a legal-entity contact.

concepts.name: contact.email
concepts.definition: Email address recorded for a service-site contact; trim without treating it as a legal-entity contact.

decisions.name: address.type
decisions.reason: ACNC discovery has Address_Type=Business (row 2), and user guide p. 2 identifies the bundled fields as charity business-address details; the address-role category is distinct from address.full.

decisions.name: address.line_1
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 2 lists Address line 1 as a separate business-address component, distinct from the existing complete address.full claim.

decisions.name: address.line_2
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 2 lists Address line 2 separately; discovery rows show this component can be blank or populated while the address record stays bundled.

decisions.name: address.line_3
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 2 lists Address line 3 separately and notes it is blank for many charities, supporting an optional component rather than a duplicate of address.full.

decisions.name: registration.acnc_date_registered
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 2 defines Registration date as the effective ACNC registration date; this regulator-specific event is distinct from generic/company registration dates.

decisions.name: entity.date_established
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 3 says Date organisation established records when the charity was established and may precede registration; discovery also supplies it separately from Registration_Date.

decisions.name: entity.charity_size
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 3 defines size from the latest Annual Information Statement and documents Small, Medium, and Large categories; the definition preserves this source-reported context.

decisions.name: entity.responsible_person_count
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 3 defines the field as the number of board or committee members and explicitly says zero means the charity did not supply the information; non-negative parsing is implementable with the documented zero sentinel handled by mapping conditions.

decisions.name: financial_period.year_end
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 3 defines Financial Year End and gives examples including 30 June and 31 December; a month-day string preserves the source label without inventing a year.

decisions.name: entity.operating_region
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 4 states that affirmative Y indicators identify operating states/territories and blanks mean no indicator; the many-valued category fits multiple independently observed affirmative regions.

decisions.name: entity.operating_country
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 4 specifies comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes for overseas operating locations; splitting codes is a declarative transformation and preserves multiple source claims.

decisions.name: entity.charity_subtype
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 5 enumerates the subtype indicators, including charitable purposes, PBI, and HPC, and says Y denotes a registered subtype; the category set is source-defined and multi-valued.

decisions.name: entity.charity_beneficiary_category
decisions.reason: ACNC user guide p. 6 lists the beneficiary categories and states Y denotes a group the charity reports assisting; the definition correctly avoids turning blank fields into negative claims.

decisions.name: licence.number
decisions.reason: ASIC AFS Licensee Help File p. 8 defines AFS_LIC_NUM as the unique identifying number allocated to a licensee; retaining it as a string avoids losing identifier formatting.

decisions.name: licence.register_entry_name
decisions.reason: ASIC AFS Licensee Help File p. 8 says AFS_LIC_NAME is the register entry name, displayed as a person's name or an organisation name; the licence scope avoids asserting legal-name ownership.

decisions.name: licence.start_date
decisions.reason: ASIC AFS Licensee Help File p. 8 defines AFS_LIC_START_DT as the start date of the AFS licensee; keeping it licence-scoped distinguishes it from company registration.

decisions.name: licence.pre_fsr_reference
decisions.reason: ASIC AFS Licensee Help File p. 9 defines AFS_LIC_PRE_FSR as previous register type and licence number, permits multiple references separated by tildes, and describes their quoted encoding; source-preserving string observations are implementable.

decisions.name: licence.authorisation_condition
decisions.reason: ASIC AFS Licensee Help File p. 11 defines AFS_LIC_CONDITION as current authorised services/products and documents tilde-separated condition lines or rows; separate licence-scoped raw observations preserve that meaning.

decisions.name: registration.registered_business_name
decisions.reason: ASIC Business Names Help File p. 8 defines BN_NAME as the name used in relation to one or more businesses as shown on the register; the definition does not infer a legal-entity owner.

decisions.name: registration.business_name_status
decisions.reason: ASIC Business Names Help File pp. 8–9 defines registration status and Registered/Cancelled labels; the publisher notes also describe deregistered names, and discovery includes Deregistered, so retaining source labels avoids conflating this with entity.status.

decisions.name: registration.business_name_registration_date
decisions.reason: ASIC Business Names Help File p. 9 defines BN_REG_DT as the date by which the business name started and specifies DD/MM/YYYY; the definition distinguishes it from company registration.

decisions.name: registration.business_name_cancellation_date
decisions.reason: ASIC Business Names Help File p. 9 defines BN_CANCEL_DT as the date the business name ceased when supplied; the definition appropriately distinguishes it from entity deregistration.

decisions.name: registration.former_state_number
decisions.reason: ASIC Business Names Help File p. 9 defines BN_STATE_NUM as a former business-name identifier allocated by a prior state or territory regulator; preserving the source string fits its variable format.

decisions.name: registration.previous_state_of_registration
decisions.reason: ASIC Business Names Help File p. 9 defines BN_STATE_OF_REG as the former regulator's state and enumerates the abbreviations; the proposed enum matches that documented set.

decisions.name: registration.business_name_abn
decisions.reason: ASIC Business Names Help File p. 10 defines BN_ABN as an ABN shown on a business-name record and documents nulls for suppressed, former-regulator, or multiple ABNs; entry-level scope and no ownership inference are appropriate.

decisions.name: entity.asic_company_type
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File p. 8 defines Type and documents APTY, APUB, FNOS, and RACN; preserving the register's specific codes avoids overloading the broader entity.entity_type.

decisions.name: entity.asic_company_class
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File pp. 8–9 defines Class as company liability class and documents the proposed codes; this is distinct from entity.entity_type.

decisions.name: entity.asic_company_sub_class
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File pp. 9–10 defines Sub Class and enumerates the proposed company subclass codes; retaining them separately is source-faithful.

decisions.name: entity.asic_register_status
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File pp. 10–11 documents the status codes and their distinct meanings; preserving these codes avoids asserting a one-to-one translation into entity.status.

decisions.name: registration.original_state
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File p. 11 defines Previous State of Registration as the state where the company was originally registered; registration scope distinguishes it from address.state.

decisions.name: registration.state_registration_number
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File p. 11 defines the state registration number as the number assigned on original state registration and says formats vary by state; string storage is appropriate.

decisions.name: registration.company_deregistration_date
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File p. 11 defines Date of Deregistration as the date the company was deregistered; the scoped concept avoids merging distinct registration regimes.

decisions.name: entity.current_name_indicator
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File p. 11 says the indicator is Y or null, but this definition requires mapping blank to an unknown boolean claim; the trusted engine emits no claim for blank values, so that specified behavior is not implementable as stated.

decisions.name: registration.current_name_start_date
decisions.reason: ASIC Company Dataset Help File p. 12 defines Current Name Start Date as the start date for the current registered company name; its registration context distinguishes it from company registration date.

decisions.name: financial_period.reporting_period
decisions.reason: Corporate Tax Transparency discovery includes Income year values such as 2023-24, and dataset notes identify reported corporate tax information by income year; retaining the label as supplied avoids unsupported period conversion.

decisions.name: service_location.code
decisions.reason: Employment Services dataset notes describe service-location information, and discovery provides DIS_SITE_CODE values such as A230; preserving the source identifier as a location-scoped string avoids entity-identity inference.

decisions.name: service_location.contract_name
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery has CONTRACT_NAME values such as DESB on location rows, while dataset notes describe service locations; recording the label in that row context does not assert a legal contract relationship.

decisions.name: service_location.name
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery has LOCATION_NAME values such as CANBERRA and dataset notes identify location information; the location scope distinguishes this label from an entity name.

decisions.name: service_location.address_line
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery labels SITE_ADDRESS_LN and supplies site street-address values; dataset notes describe location information, supporting a location-scoped line without inferred components.

decisions.name: service_location.website
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery labels SITE_URL and supplies website values; the location-scoped definition avoids treating the URL as an entity-wide website.

decisions.name: service_location.latitude
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery supplies LATITUDE values such as -35.2791945; decimal storage with the documented geographic latitude bounds is implementable and location-scoped.

decisions.name: service_location.longitude
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery supplies LONGITUDE values such as 149.1306937; decimal storage with the documented geographic longitude bounds is implementable and location-scoped.

decisions.name: service_location.agent_freecall_phone
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery explicitly labels AGENT_FREECALL_NUM and supplies telephone-like values; retaining the number as a location-scoped string preserves leading zeros and distinguishes this role.

decisions.name: contact.phone
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery explicitly labels SITE_CONTACT_PHONE and shows phone values; the definition preserves it as a site-contact claim rather than an entity-wide contact.

decisions.name: contact.email
decisions.reason: Employment Services discovery explicitly labels SITE_EMAIL_ADDRESS and shows email values; contact scope and the stated site context avoid asserting a legal-entity contact.

Page 1 of 6 
 
 
OFFICIAL 
OFFICIAL 
 
 
Purpose 
These explanatory notes explain the ‘Registered Charities’ dataset, and the ‘data outputs’ that you can 
expect for each field. 
This document was updated in December 2024. 
 
 
Background 
1. The Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) was established on 3 December 2012. 
2. The Registered Charities dataset is a subset of the information available on the ACNC Charity Register, 
and is based on a variety of sources. It includes data provided by charities:  
• when they first registered with the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) (who subsequently provided 
this information to the ACNC), 
• when registering with the ACNC, 
• who update details via the ACNC Charity Portal 
• via the Annual Information Statement. 
3. To view more information on individual charities (including governing documents or any financial 
reports), search the ACNC Charity Register using the charity’s legal name or ABN.  
4. This dataset is updated weekly, and only includes data from charities registered with the ACNC. 
5. Registered charities can apply to the ACNC to have some or all of the information they provide withheld 
from the ACNC Register (www.acnc.gov.au/withhold). If data has been withheld, the relevant data  (or 
entire charity record) will be excluded from the dataset. 
 
 
 
Australian Charities and 
Not-For-Profits Commission 
User guide – Registered Charities Dataset

Page 2 of 6 
 
 
OFFICIAL 
OFFICIAL 
Data outputs 
Charity details 
ABN (column A) 
6. This is a charity’s Australian Business Number (ABN). To register with the ACNC, charities must have an 
ABN. Organisations apply for an ABN through the Australian Business Register, and must meet certain 
conditions to do so (http://abr.gov.au). 
7. Each charity will have an ABN (unless the charity’s ABN is withheld) and all data in this field is numeric. 
Charity name (column B) 
8. This is a charity’s formal name as it appears on legal or official documents. This field is pre-populated 
based on the legal name the charity provides on registration , except where the charity’s legal 
name is withheld. In some cases where the charity’s legal name is withheld, an alternate identifier 
may be substituted by the ACNC. 
9. The data in this field is free text, and can contain numbers, letters and punctuation symbols.  
Other organisation names (column C) 
10. In some cases, a charity might have one or more trading names, or other names. These might be similar 
or completely different to their legal name, and are often the name(s) by which the charity is best 
known in the general community. 
11. The data in this field is free text, and can contain numbers, letters and punctuation symbols. If the field 
is blank, it means that the charity did not provide any other name , or it is withheld. 
Charity address (columns D-K) 
12. This is the charity’s business address (the street address that the charity operates from). 
13. The fields relating to this question are: 
• Address line 1 
• Address line 2 
• Address line 3 
• Town/City 
• State 
• Postcode 
• Country 
14. These fields contain the business address details provided by each charity. Where a field is blank, it 
means that no information was provided by the charity for that particular field or is withheld . The 
‘Address line 3’ field is blank for many charities. 
Charity w ebsite – (column L) 
15. This field contains the charity’s website address (where supplied). 
Registration date (column M) 
16. This field contains the effective date that the charity was registered with the ACNC. 
17. For charities that were registered for tax concessions prior to the establishment of the ACNC, this date 
will automatically be 3 December 2012 (the date the ACNC commenced).

Page 3 of 6 
 
 
OFFICIAL 
OFFICIAL 
Date organisation established (column N) 
18. This field contains the date that the charity was established. Some organisations run as not-for-profits 
for years before deciding to register as charities.  
Charity size (column O) 
19. Charities have different reporting obligations to the ACNC depending on their annual revenue: 
 
Size Pre-2022 thresholds Post-2022 thresholds 
Small Revenue less than $250,000 Revenue less than $500,000 
Medium Revenue $250,000 or over but 
under $1 million 
Revenue of $500,000 or over but 
under $ 3 million 
Large Revenue of $1 million or more Revenue of $3 million or more 
 
20. This field is based on the latest Annual Information Statement submitted by the charity. 
21. A blank field indicates that the charity has not yet submitted an Annual Information Statement or this data is 
withheld. 
Number of responsible persons (column P) 
22. This field shows the number of board members or committee members that the charity has. A zero in 
this field indicates that a charity has not supplied this information.  
Financial Year End (column Q) 
23. This field shows the financial year end of the charity. 
24. Charities may apply to the ACNC to have a financial year end other than 30 June. For instance, many 
schools work to a financial year end of 31 December.

Page 4 of 6 
 
 
OFFICIAL 
OFFICIAL 
Charity operating locations 
Operating locations (columns R- Z) 
25. Charities are asked to provide their operating locations. The fields relating to this question are: 
• Operates in ACT 
• Operates in NSW 
• Operates in NT 
• Operates in QLD 
• Operates in SA 
• Operates in TAS 
• Operates in VIC 
• Operates in WA 
• Operates overseas. 
26. If a charity indicated that they operated in a state or territory, a ‘Y’ will be recorded in the column for 
the relevant state or territory. If they did not operate in the state or territory, the field will be blank. 
27. If the charity operates overseas, column Z (‘Operating Countries’) will contain data. The information in 
this field is based on the ISO 3166-1 alpha 3 codes, which can be found at 
http://www.iso.org/iso/country_codes.htm .   
28. Where a charity operates in more than one overseas location, there will be multiple country codes 
separated by a comma (e.g. BRA, KHM, TCD  stands for Brazil, Cambodia and Chad).

Page 5 of 6 
 
 
OFFICIAL 
OFFICIAL 
Charity subtypes 
Subtypes (columns AA-AN) 
29. Charities be registered with one or more charity ‘subtypes’. These subtypes are categories that reflect 
the charity’s charitable purpose, for example ‘advancing education’ or ‘advancing health’. A charity’s 
purpose is the reason it has been set up, or what its activities work towards achieving.  
30. Our Act sets out 14 charity subtypes. These include the 12 charitable purposes as set out in the 
Charities Act 2013 (Cth), as well as the categories Public Benevolent Institution (PBI) and Health 
Promotion Charity (HPC). 
31. The fields include: 
• PBI 
• HPC 
• Preventing or relieving suffering of animals 
• Advancing Culture 
• Advancing Education 
• Advancing Health 
• Promote or oppose a change to law government poll or prac[tice] 
• Advancing natural environment 
• Promoting or protecting human rights 
• Purposes beneficial to the general public and other analogous 
• Promoting reconciliation mutual respect and tolerance 
• Advancing Religion 
• Advancing social or public welfare 
• Advancing security or safety of Australia or Australian public 
32. If a charity is registered with a subtype, a ‘Y’ will be recorded in the column for the relevant subtype 
(unless this data is withheld). Otherwise, the field will be blank.

Page 6 of 6 
 
 
OFFICIAL 
OFFICIAL 
Charity beneficiaries 
Beneficiaries (columns AO-BQ) 
 
33. Charities are able to nominate one or more beneficiaries from the following list: 
• Aboriginal or TSI 
• Adults 
• Aged Persons 
• Children 
• Communities Overseas 
• Early Childhood 
• Ethnic Groups 
• Families 
• Females 
• Financially Disadvantaged 
• LGBTIQA+ 
• General Community in Australia 
• Males 
• Migrants Refugees or Asylum Seekers 
• Other Beneficiaries 
• Other Charities 
• People at risk of homelessness 
• People with Chronic Illness 
• People with Disabilities 
• Pre Post Release Offenders 
• Rural Regional Remote Communities 
• Unemployed Person 
• Veterans or their families 
• Victims of crime 
• Victims of Disasters 
• Youth 
• Animals 
• Environment 
• Other gender identities 
34. If a charity has reported that they assist a beneficiary group, a ‘Y’ will be recorded in the column for the 
relevant beneficiary (unless this data is withheld). Otherwise, the field will be blank.

###_NOTE: This dataset is updated weekly. Please ensure that you use the most up-to-date version._###

The Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) is the national regulator of charities in Australia. 

Since 3 December 2012, charities wanting to access Commonwealth charity tax concessions (and other benefits), need to register with the ACNC. Although many charities choose to register, registration with the ACNC is voluntary. 

The ACNC maintains a register (known as the Charity Register), which contains information about charities. This dataset is a subset of the information available on the Charity Register.

Additional information for each charity (including governing documents and names of any Responsible Persons) can be found by searching the Charity Register at [acnc.gov.au/charity](https://www.acnc.gov.au/charity).

In some situations, charities can apply to have some or all of their information withheld from the Charity Register.  If the ACNC has approved for the information to be withheld, it won’t appear on the Charity Register, or in this dataset. 

Each year, charities also lodge Annual Information Statements with the ACNC. These record further information about charities’ purposes, activities and operations for the year - the ACNC publishes datasets for each Annual Information Statement. 

PLEASE NOTE: It is possible that some information in this dataset might be subject to a future request by the charity to have their information withheld, but will still appear in the dataset until the next update. Please consider this risk when using this dataset. 

Please use the attached explanatory notes to help with analysis of this dataset.

commas. 
The Business Names Dataset csv uses the 'TAB' character as the delimiter (value separator) between 
values in the dataset; the 'TAB' character is used in place of a comma separator because business names

Getting Started 
1. Purpose 
ASIC successfully made its Company register extract available to the public via data.gov.au on the 3 
September 2014. This document is to provide detailed context and understanding of the files uploaded 
to Data.gov.au by ASIC every Tuesday. 
 
2. Company Register 
Select data from the ASIC's Company Register will be uploaded every Tuesday to www.data.gov.au. The 
data made available will be a snapshot of the register at a point in time. As a result, the information 
might not be accurate at the time you check this dataset. ASIC Connect updates information in real time, 
so please consider accessing information on that platform if you need precise information. Legislation 
prescribes the type of information ASIC is allowed to disclose to the public. 
 
The company register dataset contains the following: 
• Select fields that are publicly available (see data dictionary for field details); 
• All currently registered companies that are able to be upload to data.gov.au; 
• Deregistered companies for the past year; and 
• Historical name data for registered companies. 
 
2.1. File Format 
The company dataset is provided in a file with the extension of CSV (comma separated values) and ZIP 
that contains the CSV file inside. 
Important note: The data contained within the company register csv is not separated by commas 
The company register csv uses the 'TAB' character as the delimiter (value separator) between values in 
the dataset; the 'TAB' character is used in place of a comma separator because company names can 
contain commas in their name and therefore is not a suitable delimiter for this dataset.

###Update March 2025 ###

From 11 March 2025, the dataset will be updated to include 1 new field, Date of Deregistration, (see help file for details). 

###Update August 2018 - frequency change to Company dataset ###

From 7 August 2018, the Company dataset will be updated weekly every Tuesday. As a result, the information might not be accurate at the time you check the Company dataset.
[ASIC-Connect](https://connectonline.asic.gov.au/ "ASIC-Connect") updates information in real time, therefore, please consider accessing information on that platform if you need up to date information.

***

###Dataset summary###
ASIC is Australia’s corporate, markets and financial services regulator. ASIC contributes to Australia’s economic reputation and wellbeing by ensuring that Australia’s financial markets are fair and transparent, supported by confident and informed investors and consumers.

Australian companies are required to keep their details up to date on ASIC's Company Register. Information contained in the register is made available to the public to search via ASIC's website.

Select data from the ASIC's Company Register will be uploaded each week to www.data.gov.au. The data made available will be a snapshot of the register at a point in time. Legislation prescribes the type of information ASIC is allowed to disclose to the public.

The information included in the downloadable dataset is:

* Company Name
* Australian Company Number (ACN)
* Type 
* Class
* Sub Class 
* Status
* Date of Registration
* Date of Deregistration (Available from 11 March 2025)
* Previous State of Registration (where applicable)
* State Registration Number (where applicable) 
* Modified since last report – flag to indicate if data has been modified since last report
* Current Name Indicator
* Australian Business Number (ABN) 
* Current Name
* Current Name Start Date

Additional information about companies can be found via [ASIC's website](http://www.asic.gov.au/ "ASIC website"). Accessing some information may attract a fee.

More information about searching [ASIC's registers](http://www.asic.gov.au/online-services/search-asics-registers/ "ASIC registers").
***

These reports contain the name, ABN, total income, taxable income and tax payable for corporate tax entities with a total income of $100 million or more. This includes Australian public and foreign-owned corporate tax entities and Australian-owned resident private companies.

For the 2021-22 and earlier income years, the reports include details for • Australian public and foreign-owned corporate tax entities with a total income of $100 million or more; and • Australian-owned resident private companies with a total income of $200 million or more.

They also contain the name, ABN and tax payable for any entity that has a petroleum resource rent tax (PRRT) payable amount. Entities that had minerals resource rent tax (MRRT) payable were included for the 2013-14 and 2014-15 MRRT years only.
